docs.text:
1. Expand Combat Attack System.
  2. Set Initial Attack Delay to 3 seconds and Combat Distance to 100.
  3. Set Phase 0 Health Range: Min Health = 50, Max Health = 100.
  4. Set Group 0 Distance: 0 to 5 meters.
  5. Configure ability flags & selection memory:
  6. Do Not Repeat Last: Checked (Prevents repeating the single most recent ability).
  7. Recent Ability Memory: Set to 3 (Keeps track of recently used abilities to ensure random variance).
  8. Set Probability Sliders to 100% for:
  9. Melee Attack
  10. Ground Slam
  11. Spit Attack
  12. Teleportation

docs.title: Step 3.2: Mid Range Group (6 - 30 meters)
docs.text:
1. Click Add Distance Group.
  2. Set Distance to 6 to 30 meters.
  3. Set Min/Max Attack Delay to 2 seconds.
  4. Adjust Ability Probabilities:
  5. Melee Attack: 80%
  6. Ground Slam: 30%
  7. Flamethrower: 80%
  8. Charging Attack: 100% (Highest Priority)
  9. Teleportation: 70%
  10. Spit Attack: 0% (Disabled for mid-range)

docs.title: Step 3.3: Long Range Group (31 - 100 meters)
docs.text:
1. Click Add Distance Group.
  2. Set Distance to 31 to 100 meters (or 7 to 100).
  3. Enable Summon Minions and adjust ranged parameters (e.g., Meteor Strike, Projectiles).

docs.title: 4. Setting Up Combo Chain Attacks
docs.text:
Chain attacks trigger follow-up abilities automatically without waiting for combat selection cycles.

[ Primary Attack (Melee) ] │ (0.6s Transition Delay) ▼ [ Chain Attack 1 (Ground Slam) ] │ (0.6s Transition Delay) ▼ [ Chain Attack 2 (Flamethrower) ]

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Under Group 0 (0-5m), expand Melee Attack.
  2. Check Enable Chain Attack.
  3. Expand Chain Attack 1:
  4. Chain Transition Delay: 0.6 seconds.
  5. Target Ability: Select Ground Slam.
  6. Expand Ground Slam parameters and check Enable Chain Attack:
  7. Chain Attack Count: 1.
  8. Chain Transition Delay: 0.6 seconds.
  9. Target Ability: Select Flamethrower.
  10. Under Group 1 (6-30m), expand Teleportation:
  11. Check Enable Chain Attack.
  12. Chain Transition Delay: 0.5 seconds.
  13. Target Ability: Select Meteor Strike with 100% probability.

docs.title: 5. Multi-Phase Combat (Phase 1 Layer)
docs.text: Scale aggressiveness when the boss drops below half health.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. In the Enemy Ability System, click Add Phase Layer. This copies all existing distance groups into Phase 1.
  2. Configure Phase 1 Health Range:
  3. Min Health: 0
  4. Max Health: 50
  5. Decrease Min/Max Attack Delay across all Phase 1 groups to 1 second to accelerate attack frequency.

docs.title: 6. Camera States & Sound Hooks Setup
docs.text: Bind boss lifecycle events to camera modes and global sound effects.

docs.title: Step 6.1: Boss Camera Tracking Activation
docs.text:
1. Select Bull Boss New and expand Global Event Hooks.
  2. Add two new global events:
  3. Event 1 (On Start): Drag Camera Rig -> Select MouseCameraRotation.ActivateBossCamera.
  4. Event 2 (On Dying): Drag Camera Rig -> Select MouseCameraRotation.DeactivateBossCamera.

docs.title: Step 6.2: On-Hit Universal Audio Player Setup
docs.text:
1. Select Boss Voice Controller and remove the on hit entry from categories.
  2. Select Bull Boss New -> expand Universal Sound Player.
  3. Create an action entry named hit sounds and populate it with hit audio clips.
  4. Under Global Event Hooks:
  5. Map On Take Damage to Universal Sound Player -> Select UniversalSoundPlayer.PlayAudioCategory.
  6. Pass string parameter: hit sounds.
  7. Under Boss Voice Controller, set in combat voice clip cooldown to 8 seconds.

docs.title: Batch Animator Transition Tool
docs.text:
1. Navigate to Tools -> Boss AI Toolkit -> Animator Transition Tool.
  2. Drag the boss's Animator Controller into the field.
  3. Set New Duration to 0.3 seconds.
  4. Click Apply Transition Duration to smooth out transitions across all states.

docs.title: Ability Copy-Paste Feature
docs.text:
1. Modify ability parameters (e.g., adjust Ground Slam Range or Flamethrower Rotation Speed).
  2. Right-click the modified ability context header and select Copy Ability.
  3. Expand target distance groups/phases, right-click, and select Paste Ability.

docs.title: 8. Verification Checklist
docs.text:
Before testing in Play Mode, check the following configuration settings:

  • [ ] Rotation Delay: Smooth Look Rotation Delay set to 2 seconds.
  • [ ] Pre-Combat State: Enable Pre-Combat toggled off for immediate engagement.
  • [ ] Distance Groups: Proper distance brackets (0-5m, 6-30m, 31-100m) configured under Phase 0.
  • [ ] Combo Connections: Enable Chain Attack verified for Melee -> Ground Slam -> Flamethrower.
  • [ ] Phase 1 Settings: Health limits (0-50 HP) set with attack delay dropped to 1 second.
  • [ ] Global Events: Camera activation bound to On Start/On Dying and hit sounds bound to On Take Damage.
  • [ ] Animator Transitions: Transition duration updated to 0.3 seconds across states.

docs.title: Player Vs Spider Boss Setup
docs.text: This setup provides a guide to setting up and configuring the Spider Boss using assets from the Mobile Spider and Worm Pack in Unity. It details how to clone configuration settings from an existing boss (such as the Bull Boss), swap/replace animations, reassign body nodes and visual components, configure specialized abilities, and set up hitbox collision.

docs.title: 1. Initial Scene Setup
docs.text: Import and unpack the spider model and set up the duplication base.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Navigate to Mobile Spider and Worm Pack > Spider > FBX in the Project window and drag the spider model into your scene hierarchy.
  2. Apply your preferred texture (e.g., fire texture).
  3. Right-click the spider GameObject in the hierarchy and select Prefab > Unpack Completely.
  4. Duplicate the existing Bull Boss New GameObject in the hierarchy to serve as the cloning source, then deactivate the original.

docs.title: 2. Cloning Boss AI Configuration
docs.text: Transfer components, scripts, and settings from the source boss to the spider using the toolkit cloning tool.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Navigate to the top menu: Tools > Boss AI Toolkit > Duplicate Enemy.
  2. Configure the tool parameters:
  3. Source Boss: Drag in the duplicated Bull Boss New GameObject.
  4. Target Boss: Drag in the unpacked Spider GameObject (rename it to Spider Boss).
  5. Target Avatar: Select and assign the Spider Avatar from the project files.
  6. Click Start Cloning Configuration and close the window upon completion.

docs.title: 3. Hierarchy & Visual GameObjects Transfer
docs.text:
Re-parent child GameObjects and attach effect origins to the spider rig.

Spider Boss (Root) ├── Spider Rig / Bones │ └── Neck / Head Bone │ └── Flamethrower Visual Effect Object └── Projectiles / Effects (Transferred from Bull Boss) ├── Shockwave Effect ├── Stone / Rock Object └── Teleportation Visual Effects

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Snap the position of Spider Boss to match Bull Boss New.
  2. Move necessary child objects (effects, projectiles, stones) from the Bull Boss hierarchy to Spider Boss.
  3. Attach the Flamethrower effect object to the spider's neck bone (Spider Rig > Neck).
  4. Remove unneeded weapon GameObjects transferred from the Bull Boss.
  5. Delete the empty Bull Boss source hierarchy from the scene.

docs.title: 4. Animator & Animation Replacement
docs.text: Duplicate the controller and substitute animation clips using the Animator Clip Replacer tool.

docs.title: Step 4.1: Controller Setup
docs.text:
1. Duplicate the source Animator Controller asset in the Project window and rename it to Spider Boss Animator Controller.
  2. Assign Spider Boss Animator Controller to the Animator component on Spider Boss.

docs.title: Step 4.2: Replacing Clips
docs.text:
1. Open Tools > Boss AI Toolkit > Animator Clip Replacer.
  2. Assign the Spider Boss Animator Controller.
  3. Replace the Bull Boss clips with corresponding Spider FBX clips:
  4. Idle -> Spider Idle
  5. Walking/Movement -> Spider Crawl Backward (Set clip speed to -1 in the Animator to make it walk forward)
  6. Hit Reactions -> Assign Hit 1 to hit reaction one and hit reaction two.
  7. Remove unused weapon state nodes (e.g., Equipped Weapon, Unequipped Weapon).
  8. Uncheck IK Pass on the Animator layer if hand/foot IK is not required.

docs.title: 5. Dissolve & Teleportation Material Setup
docs.text: Reconfigure skin mesh renderers and dissolve materials for teleportation and spawn/death FX.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Select Spider Boss and expand the Enemy Dissolve Controller component.
  2. Remove weapon dissolve entries from the array.
  3. Configure skin dissolve entries:
  4. Skin Mesh Renderer: Drag in the Spider Rig Skinned Mesh Renderer.
  5. Renderer Type: Set to Skinned Mesh Renderer.
  6. Original Material: Assign the default spider material.
  7. Dissolve Material: Assign the spider-specific dissolve material.

docs.title: 6. Global Settings & Ability Adjustments
docs.text: Fine-tune movement, rotation, and custom ability parameters for the spider model.

docs.title: Global & UI Parameter Tuning
docs.text: Parameter Recommended Value Description Rotation Speed 300 Adjusts turning speed for spider movement. Smooth Look Rotation Delay 2.0 seconds Delay window allowing player attacks before boss tracks. Rotate Spine Bone Unchecked Disabled since the spider does not utilize a single spine pivot. Hit Interval (Min / Max) 2 / 2 seconds Cooldown interval between hit reactions.

docs.title: Teleportation Ability Tuning
docs.text:
1. Register custom clips using the Animation Setup Tool:
  2. Add Get In Ground (Parameter Name: get in ground)
  3. Add Get Out Of Ground (Parameter Name: get out of ground)
  4. Under Teleportation Ability:
  5. Set Disappear Animation to get out of ground.
  6. Set Appear Animation to get in ground.
  7. Enable Spawn Behind Target.
  8. Assign teleportation particle effects and set Idle Delay to 0.

docs.title: Flamethrower Ability Tuning
docs.text:
• Set Rotation Mode to Rotate Full Body.
  • Assign the head/neck-mounted flamethrower particle origin.
  • Set Rotation Speed to 50 and Spine Rotation Speed to 0.

docs.title: 7. Hitbox Controller Setup
docs.text: Configure manual hitboxes to deal damage during attack animations.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Create a child GameObject named Hitbox under Spider Boss.
  2. Add a Capsule Collider component, adjust its bounds over the spider's attack area, and check Is Trigger.
  3. Add the Hitbox script component:
  4. Damage Value: Set desired damage output.
  5. Owner: Drag the Spider Boss reference.
  6. Team Member: Assign the team member reference script.
  7. Activation Mode: Set to Manual.
  8. Check Deactivate Hitbox On Hit and Deactivate Hitbox After Time.
  9. Open the Unity Animation Window, select attack clips (duplicate clips if read-only), and add animation events:
  10. Start of attack frame: Call HitboxController.ActivateHitbox().
  11. End of attack frame: Call HitboxController.DeactivateHitbox().

docs.title: 8. Verification Checklist
docs.text:
Before running tests in Play Mode, check the following configuration settings:

  • [ ] Cloned Configuration: Settings cloned from source boss and avatar assigned.
  • [ ] Animator Assigned: Duplicated Spider Boss Animator Controller assigned.
  • [ ] Forward Walk Animation: Backward crawl animation speed set to -1 in the Animator.
  • [ ] Hierarchy Re-parented: Visual effects (flamethrower, ground slam) parented to the spider rig.
  • [ ] Dissolve Materials Mapped: Skinned mesh renderer and spider dissolve materials linked.
  • [ ] Hitbox Events Configured: Animation events set to trigger and deactivate hitboxes during attack animations.

docs.title: Player Setup
docs.text: This setup provides a comprehensive guide on migrating components, logic, weapons, animations, hitboxes, and visual effects from the default toolkit player to a custom 3D player model using the Boss AI Toolkit Player Setup Wizard in Unity.

docs.title: 1. Automated Player Migration (Player Setup Wizard)
docs.text: Use the built-in wizard tool to quickly transfer components, scripts, hitboxes, and bone references from an existing template player to a new custom player model.

docs.title: Step 1.1: Preparing the Model
docs.text:
1. Place your new 3D player model into the scene hierarchy and name it Player New
  2. Align its position and rotation to match the original template player
  3. Apply the appropriate player material to the mesh
  4. Right-click Player New and create a child empty GameObject named Hit Point Position it around the chest/torso area

docs.title: Step 1.2: Running the Setup Wizard
docs.text:
1. Navigate to Tools -> Boss AI Toolkit -> Player Setup
  2. Assign the fields as follows:
  3. Source Player: Drag the original template player GameObject
  4. Target Player: Drag Player New
  5. New Rig: Drag the rig transform of the new player
  6. New Skinned Mesh Renderer: Drag the Skinned Mesh Renderer of the new player
  7. Hit Point: Drag the newly created Hit Point transform
  8. Weapon Parent: Drag the Right Hand bone transform
  9. Shield Parent: Drag the Left Hand bone transform
  10. Add equipment entries:
  11. Weapon List: Add element and assign Player Sword
  12. Shield List: Add element and assign Shield 2
  13. Click Apply Changes to Target Player
  14. Click Awesome when prompted

docs.title: 2. Equipment Transforms & Materials Alignment
docs.text: After running the wizard, manually adjust equipment positions, scales, and materials to fit the new character mesh.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Select the spawned sword object under the right hand:
  2. Copy the transform values (Position, Rotation, Scale) from the template weapon and paste them onto the new sword
  3. Assign the sword material
  4. Select the spawned shield object under the left hand:
  5. Copy and paste the transform values from the template shield
  6. Assign the shield material
  7. Add Navigation Cutout Avoidance:
  8. Add a Nav Mesh Modifier component to both the sword and shield GameObjects
  9. Set Mode to Remove Object
  10. NOTE: This prevents weapons from creating holes in the NavMesh during baking, which blocks Boss AI navigation

docs.title: 3. Animation Overrides & Animator Replacement
docs.text: Replace standard animation clips (e.g., Idle, Walk, Attack) with custom animations using the Animator Clip Replacer.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. In the Project window, locate Player Test Animator Controller
  2. Duplicate it (Ctrl + D or Cmd + D) and rename the copy to Player New Animator Controller
  3. Assign Player New Animator Controller to the Animator component on Player New
  4. Go to Tools -> Boss AI Toolkit -> Animator Clip Replacer
  5. Drag Player New Animator Controller into the script field
  6. Swap desired animation clips (e.g., replace Idle 5 with Idle 02)
  7. Click Apply Animator Overrides

docs.title: 4. Player Controller & UI Reference Bindings
docs.text: Rebind scene references in the Player Controller and UI Canvas to direct control to the new player entity.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Select Player New and locate the Player Controller component
  2. Update the following fields:
  3. Player Reference: Replace references pointing to the old player with Player New
  4. Hit Point: Assign Player New/Hit Point
  5. Set up the Shield Hit Point:
  6. Duplicate Hit Point, parent it under the Shield GameObject, reset its transform, and position it on the front face of the shield
  7. Assign this transform to Shield Hit Effect Spawn Point on the controller
  8. UI Canvas Update: Select the Canvas 2D object in the hierarchy and re-assign Player New to any player reference slots (e.g., Shield Button)

docs.title: 5. Melee Hitbox & Team Configuration
docs.text: Set up manual hitboxes on weapons to accurately trigger and apply damage to enemy entities.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Under Player New -> Right Hand -> Sword, create an empty child GameObject named Hitbox
  2. Add a Capsule Collider, adjust its size to cover the blade, and check Is Trigger
  3. Add the Hitbox script and configure as follows:
  4. Damage: 3
  5. Owner: Player New
  6. Compare Enemy: Checked
  7. Script Team Member: Drag Team Member script from Player New
  8. Activation Mode: Manual
  9. Deactivate Hitbox On Hit: Checked (Prevents multi-hit damage on single swings)
  10. Deactivate Hitbox After Certain Time: Checked
  11. Hitbox Lifetime: 3 seconds
  12. On Player New:
  13. Drag the new Hitbox into the Hitbox Controller component attack with the Player
  14. Set Team Member -> Team to Team 1
  15. Set My Body Part To Target to Hit Point

docs.title: 6. Weapon Slash VFX & Animation Events Setup
docs.text: Configure directional slash particles and animation event triggers for combat actions, hitboxes, and footstep audio.

docs.title: Step 6.1: Slash Spawn Point Setup
docs.text:
1. Right-click Player New -> Create Empty and name it Slash Spawn Point 1
  2. Position and rotate the point in front of the character (e.g., Position Y: 1.47, Rotation X: 370)
  3. Child a slash particle effect (e.g., Electro Slash) under Slash Spawn Point 1
  4. In the Slash Activation Manager on Player New:
  5. Assign Slash Spawn Point 1 to Slash Spawn Point
  6. Set Slash X Scale to negative (e.g., -1) if flipping directions for left slashes
  7. Assign the particle reference and set Activation Delay to 0.4 seconds

docs.title: Step 6.2: Animation Event Binding
docs.text:
Open Window -> Animation -> Animation:

  • Slash Activation: On attack animation clips (e.g., Left Slash), add an event at frame 0 calling SlashActivationManager.ActivateParticles passing the configuration name string
  • Hitbox Activation/Deactivation:
  • Add an event at the swing start frame calling HitboxController.ActivateHitbox
  • Add an event at the swing end frame calling HitboxController.DeactivateHitbox
  • Footstep Audio: On locomotion clips (e.g., Walk, Run), add an event at contact frames calling UniversalSoundPlayer.PlayAudioAction with parameter string "Footstep Sound"

docs.title: 7. Movement & Combat Parameter Reference
docs.text:
Configure fine-tuning parameters inside the Player Controller script:

Parameter Recommended Value Description Auto Rotate To Enemy Checked Automatically rotates player toward target upon attacking Auto Rotate Range 3 meters Detection range threshold for auto-targeting rotation Hit Animation Interval 1 second Cooldown between hit-reaction stagger animations Health Settings 100 HP (2s Change Duration) Smooth lerping duration for health UI depletion Slide To Enemy Optional Enables automatic closing distance slide toward enemy on attack

docs.title: 8. Verification Checklist
docs.text:
Before testing combat in Play Mode, verify all setups against this checklist:

  • [ ] NavMesh Modifiers: Sword and Shield have Nav Mesh Modifier set to Remove Object to prevent navigation holes
  • [ ] Team ID: Player set to Team1; Enemy entities set to Team2
  • [ ] Hitbox Flags: Deactivate Hitbox On Hit and Deactivate Hitbox After Certain Time enabled on weapon hitbox
  • [ ] Animation Events: ActivateHitbox, DeactivateHitbox, and ActivateParticles events are added on animation clips

docs.title: Pre Combat Behaviour
docs.text: This guide covers the setup process for Pre-Combat Behaviours using the Boss AI Toolkit in Unity. This covers how to configure non-offensive tactical actions—such as target-relative strafing or environment destruction—while waiting for main combat cooldowns.

docs.title: 1. Global Pre-Combat Settings
docs.text:
Select your enemy GameObject (Bull Boss New) and locate the Pre-Combat Abilities section in the Inspector.

┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│               PRE-COMBAT GLOBAL SETTINGS                │
├──────────────────────────┬─────────────────────────────┤
│ Property                 │ Recommended Default Value   │
├──────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────┤
│ Initial Pre-Combat Delay │ 2.0 s                       │
│ Min Pre-Combat Wait      │ 3.0 s (or 5.0 s for testing)│
│ Max Pre-Combat Wait      │ 3.0 s (or 5.0 s for testing)│
│ Sequential               │ Enabled (Checked)           │
│ NavMesh Search Range     │ 40.0 (Visualized by Gizmos) │
│ Stopping Distance        │ 3.0                         │
└──────────────────────────┴─────────────────────────────┘

docs.title: Parameter Explanations
docs.text:
• Initial Pre-Combat Delay: The waiting duration (in seconds) after the game starts before the AI enters its pre-combat loop.
  • Min / Max Pre-Combat Wait: The delay between consecutive pre-combat abilities. Setting this (e.g., 3-3 or 5-5) ensures a fixed resting period before triggering the next action.
  • Sequential: When enabled (✓), abilities execute in order from top to bottom. If disabled, abilities are selected randomly.
  • NavMesh Search Range: Defines the radius within which the AI looks for valid movement points or breakable objects. Can be visualized via Inspector Gizmos.
  • Stopping Distance: Distance at which the AI completes its movement relative to the target point.

docs.title: 2. Setting Up the Strafing Ability
docs.text: Strafing allows the AI to stay mobile while awaiting attack availability, switching movement direction based on target proximity.

docs.title: Step 1: Configure Ability Properties
docs.text:
Click Add Pre-Combat Ability and set up the following parameters:

  1. Ability Type: Set to Normal Ability.
  2. Move to Point: Enable (✓).
  3. Max Move Time: Set to 6 seconds (caps movement duration even if the target point is far away).
  4. Movement Radius: Set to 20.
  5. Allowed Directions: Select Left, Right, and Backward.
  6. Check Interval Seconds: Set to 2 seconds (frequency at which the AI evaluates its movement direction relative to the target).
  7. Configurations Count: Set to 3 (matching the number of allowed directions).

docs.title: Step 2: Download & Import Mixamo Animations
docs.text: Download three strafing animations from Mixamo: * Right Strafe Walking * Left Strafe Walking * Unarmed Walk Back

docs.title: Asset Import Settings
docs.text:
1. Select all three imported animation clips in Unity.
  2. Rig Tab: Change Animation Type to Humanoid and Click Apply.
  3. Animation Tab:
  4. Enable Loop Time and Loop Pose (✓).
  5. Set Based Upon (Root Transform Rotation) to Originaland Click Apply.

docs.title: Step 3: Register Animations in Animator & Script
docs.text:
1. Select Bull Boss New and expand Animation Setup Tool.
  2. Assign the clips and parameters:
Source Clip Assigned Parameter Name Left Strafe Walking Left Strafe Right Strafe Walking Right Strafe Unarmed Walk Back Walk Back
  1. Click Add to Animator and Optimize Animation Clips. (You can delete the imported raw .fbx files after optimization).
  2. Inside the Pre-Combat Ability inspector, map each direction:
Direction Configuration Matching Direction Animation to Play Move Speed Option 1 Backward Walk Back 2.0 Option 2 Right Right Strafe 2.0 Option 3 Left Left Strafe 2.0
  • Set Fallback Move Animation to Walking.
  • Set Idle Animation to Idle.

Tip (Smooth Transitions): In the Animator Controller, select the transitions originating from Any State to each strafe clip and increase Transition Duration from 0.1 to 0.5 for smoother animation blending.

docs.title: 3. Setting Up the Break Objects Ability
docs.text:
The Break Objects ability instructs the AI to locate and destroy destructible environmental props during pre-combat.

                     ┌────────────────────────┐
                     │  AI Finds Breakable    │
                     │  Object in Radius      │
                     └───────────┬────────────┘
                                 │
                                 ▼
                     ┌────────────────────────┐
                     │   Navigates to Object  │
                     │  (Walking Animation)   │
                     └───────────┬────────────┘
                                 │
                                 ▼
                     ┌────────────────────────┐
                     │ Plays Attack/Punch Anim│
                     └───────────┬────────────┘
                                 │
                                 ▼
                     ┌────────────────────────┐
                     │ Weapon Collider Hits   │
                     │  Object Trigger Box    │
                     └───────────┬────────────┘
                                 │
                                 ▼
                     ┌────────────────────────┐
                     │ Static Mesh Hidden     │
                     │  Fragments Activated   │
                     └────────────────────────┘

docs.title: Step 1: Add and Configure the Ability
docs.text:
1. Click Add Pre-Combat Ability (+).
  2. Set Ability Type to Break Objects.
  3. Check Find Closest Object (✓).
  4. Set parameters:
  5. Move Speed: 2.0
  6. Stopping Distance: 3.0
  7. Final Animation Delay: 2.0
  8. Move Animation: Walking
  9. Punch Animation: Attack 1 (Assign your melee attack clip via the Animation Setup Tool).

docs.title: Step 2: Environment Object Setup (Breakable Object)
docs.text:
For an object to be breakable by the AI, it must meet the following structural requirements:

  1. Tag: Set GameObject tag to BreakableObject.
  2. Trigger Collider: Add a Box Collider with Is Trigger enabled (✓).
  3. Script: Attach the Breakable Object script.
  4. Child Objects:
  5. Static Object: Active by default; contains the clean Mesh Renderer.
  6. Destructible Object: Inactive by default; contains individual fractured mesh pieces, each with a Rigidbody and Collider attached.
  7. Assign both references in the Breakable Object script and set Break Delay to 1.0 second.

Warning (Weapon Collider Requirement): The enemy's weapon (or attacking body part) must have an active collider (e.g., a Capsule Collider attached to a child Damage Point object). If no collider triggers the object's hit area, the break action will fail to initiate.

docs.title: Step 3: Mesh Fracturing Tool (Optional)
docs.text:
To create custom destructible models directly inside Unity:

  1. Open Tools < Boss AI Toolkit < Mesh Fracture.
  2. Drag and drop your static mesh (e.g., Stone Pillar) into the window.
  3. Set Number of Pieces:
  4. Mobile Platforms: Recommended 8 – 10 pieces max to maintain physics performance.
  5. PC / Console: Higher piece counts allowed.
  6. Click Start Fracture Process.
  7. Click Save as Mesh and choose your target directory.

docs.title: Sequential Execution Flow
docs.text:
When multiple abilities are added with Sequential enabled:

┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                        PRE-COMBAT RUNTIME FLOW                         │
├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  1. Game Start ──► Wait [Initial Pre-Combat Delay: 2s]                 │
│  2. Execute Ability 1 (e.g., Break Object 1)                          │
│  3. Wait [Pre-Combat Delay: 5s]                                        │
│  4. Execute Ability 2 (e.g., Strafing for Max 6s)                      │
│  5. Wait [Pre-Combat Delay: 5s]                                        │
│  6. Execute Ability 1 (Target next closest Breakable Object, if any)   │
│  7. If no breakable objects remain ──► Fall back to Strafing            │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

docs.title: Testing Checklist
docs.text:
• [x] Verify enemy switches from Left, Right, and Backward strafings dynamically as the player shifts positions around the enemy.
  • [x] Ensure weapon Capsule Collider properly contacts the object trigger zone.
  • [x] Adjust Break Delay value per object to sync the physical break effect precisely with the impact frame of the attack animation.

docs.title: Chase & Attack
docs.text: This part details how to set up both Ground Projectile Attacks and Aerial Projectile Attacks for the Bull Boss using the Boss AI Toolkit in Unity. It covers ability configuration, animation bindings, custom projectile prefab setup, timing logic, and flying point parameters.

docs.title: 1. Initial Ability & Spawn Point Setup
docs.text: Configure the core Projectile Attack parameters inside the Enemy Ability System and set up the origin point for projectile instantiation.

docs.title: Step 1.1: Projectile Spawn Point Creation
docs.text:
1. Right-click in the Hierarchy and select Create Empty.
  2. Name the object Projectile Spawn Point.
  3. Position the object near the boss's hand or spine (where projectiles should originate).

docs.title: Step 1.2: Core Ability Configuration
docs.text:
1. Select the Bull Boss GameObject in the scene hierarchy.
  2. Expand the Enemy Ability System component.
  3. Set previous ability probabilities (e.g., Throw Weapon) to 0% and click Add Ability Entry to Group.
  4. Set Ability Type to Projectile Attack.
  5. Set Projectile Attack Probability to 100% for isolated testing.
  6. Configure timing and targeting settings:
  7. Look Mode: Target
  8. Powerup Animation Duration: 3 seconds
  9. Projectile Throw Animation Duration: 3 seconds
  10. Look At Target While Spawning: Checked
  11. Projectile Spawn Delay: 1 second
  12. Initial Projectile Move Delay: 3 seconds
  13. Parent Spawn Projectile: Checked (ensures the projectile rotates with the boss before launching).
  14. Idle Delay: 1 second
  15. Assign the Projectile Spawn Point GameObject to the Spawn Point field.

docs.title: 2. Animation Setup
docs.text: Import and bind the power-up charge animation and projectile release animation via the Animation Setup Tool.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Open the Animation Setup Tool on the Bull Boss.
  2. Locate the animations in the project folder (Boss AI Toolkit -> Animations):
  3. Powerup Animation (power up)
  4. Spellcast / Throw Animation (projectile throw)
  5. Click Add Animation and assign both clips:
  6. Set parameter name for the powerup clip to Power Up.
  7. Set parameter name for the throw clip to Projectile Throw.
  8. Click Add to Animator.
  9. Select Bull Boss and set:
  10. Powerup Animation: Power Up
  11. Projectile Throw Animation: Projectile Throw

docs.title: 3. Projectile Prefab Configuration
docs.text: Create a custom projectile asset containing physics colliders, trajectory scripts, team detection, and damage hitboxes.

docs.title: Step 3.1: Constructing the GameObject Structure
docs.text:
1. Search for VFX Projectile 01 in the Project tab and drag it into the scene.
  2. Unpack the prefab completely and rename/nest it under an empty parent named Projectile.
  3. Unparent Projectile to place it at the scene root.

docs.title: Step 3.2: Component & Physics Setup
docs.text: Select the root Projectile object and add the following three components: 1. Sphere Collider: * Adjust radius size to fit the visual effect. * Check Is Trigger. 2. Projectile Component: * Moving Delay: 0. * Move Speed: 10. * Rotation Mode: Face Moving Direction. * Unparent On Move: Checked (detaches projectile from boss transform upon release). * Offset From Target Position: Checked. * Min / Max Offset: X=0, Y=1, Z=0. 3. Team Member Component: * Team Name: Set to match the boss's team (e.g., Team2). * My Body Part Target: Drag Projectile into this slot. 4. Hitbox Component: * Owner: Drag Projectile into this slot. * Compare Enemy: Checked. * Script Team Member: Drag the attached Team Member component here. * Activation Mode: Auto Activate On Start. * Activation Delay: 1 second. * Deactivate Hitbox On Hit: Checked. * Deactivate Hitbox After Time: Checked (5 seconds lifetime).

docs.title: Step 3.3: Link Prefab to Ability
docs.text:
1. Drag the configured Projectile object into your Prefabs folder to create a reusable asset.
  2. Delete the instance from the Hierarchy.
  3. Select Bull Boss and drag the new Projectile prefab into the Projectile Prefab field under ability settings.

docs.title: 4. Multi-Projectile Cycles & Firing Modes
docs.text: Configure how multiple projectiles are spawned and cycled during an attack sequence.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text: Set Projectile Count to 3. Choose one of the following cycle modes based on desired behavior:

docs.title: Firing Cycle Modes Comparison
docs.text: Cycle Mode Description Typical Settings Restart Cycle Plays the full Powerup and Throw animation sequence individually for each spawned projectile. Delay range: 0.1 to 0.3 seconds. Ignore Cycle Restart Plays the charge sequence once, then launches all projectiles sequentially within the same continuous cycle. Projectiles Delay: 1 second between launches.

docs.title: 5. Aerial Projectile Attack Setup
docs.text: Convert the ground attack into an aerial projectile attack where the boss leaps into the air before firing.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Right-click in Hierarchy -> Create Empty and name it Fly Point.
  2. Position Fly Point in the air.
  3. Select Bull Boss and navigate to the Projectile Attack settings:
  4. Check Fly To Point.
  5. Fly Point: Drag and drop the Fly Point GameObject.
  6. Fly Speed: Set to 3.
  7. Stay In Air Post Shoot: Set to 2 seconds (duration boss hovers after completing all projectile cycles before landing).
  8. Return Animation: Set to Idle.

docs.title: 6. Verification Checklist
docs.text:
Before running tests in Play Mode, verify all parameters against this list:

  • [ ] Spawn Point Assigned: Projectile Spawn Point is linked to the ability.
  • [ ] Unparent On Move: Enabled on the Projectile component so launched projectiles detach from the boss.
  • [ ] Team Name Match: Team Member string on the projectile matches the boss (Team2).
  • [ ] Hitbox Setup: Compare Enemy is enabled and linked to the projectile's Team Member script.
  • [ ] Aerial Fly Point: Fly To Point is checked and assigned to a valid elevated target point (if setting up aerial attacks).

docs.title: Rock Thrower Enemy Setup
docs.text: This setup provides a guide for setting up a ranged Rock Thrower Enemy using the Boss AI Toolkit in Unity. It covers FBX model preparation, configuration cloning, binding hand bone sockets for pickup animations, arc projectile setup, and fixing attack loop behaviors.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Drag the target 3D stone enemy model into the scene hierarchy.
  2. Assign the character material to the mesh renderer.
  3. Remove any pre-existing Animator component from the model.
  4. Right-click the model GameObject and select Prefab > Unpack Prefab Completely.
  5. Copy transform position values from the template Rock Thrower Enemy prefab and paste them onto the new model.
  6. Rename the model GameObject to Stone Enemy New.

docs.title: 2. Configuration Cloning
docs.text: Duplicate components, scripts, and hitboxes from the template prefab onto the new model.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Navigate to top menu: Tools > Boss AI Toolkit > Duplicate Enemy.
  2. Configure settings:
  3. Source Boss: Drag in the template Rock Thrower Enemy prefab.
  4. Target Boss: Drag in the newly prepared Stone Enemy New GameObject.
  5. New Boss Name: Set to Stone Enemy New.
  6. Target Avatar: Drag in the model's Avatar asset from the Project folder.
  7. Create New Animator Controller Asset: Uncheck (reuses template animator clips).
  8. Add Weapon: Uncheck.
  9. Click Start Cloning Configuration and close the wizard.
  10. Deactivate the original template prefab in the scene hierarchy.

docs.title: 3. Core Component & Target Mapping
docs.text: Ensure player attacks can register collisions against the enemy model.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Select Stone Enemy New in the hierarchy.
  2. Under Team Member:
  3. My Body Part To Target: Assign the enemy's root mesh object reference so player hitboxes can target.
  4. Under Enemy Ability System > Global Settings:
  5. Use Rotation Animations: Uncheck (if using standard rotation).
  6. Rotate Spine: Uncheck.

docs.title: 4. Spawner & Hand Socket Setup
docs.text: Set up the world location where rocks spawn and map the right-hand bone socket so pickup animations hold the rock accurately.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Create an empty child GameObject under Stone Enemy New named Spawn Point.
  2. Match position transform values from the template's spawn point (ground position near the feet).
  3. Select Stone Enemy New and expand Enemy Ability System > Combat Attack System.
  4. Locate the Projectile Attack ability settings:
  5. Spawn Point: Assign the Spawn Point transform.
  6. Projectile Parent: Assign the Right Hand bone transform.
    • Purpose: Parenting the spawned rock to the right hand bone ensures the rock attaches to the hand during the pickup animation before being thrown.

docs.title: 5. Combat Attack & Ability Loop Configuration
docs.text: Configure ranged engagement limits and projectile counts to ensure range checks execute properly.

docs.title: Combat Attack System
docs.text:
Parameter Recommended Value Description Phase 0 Health Range 0 - 100 Health threshold for Phase 0 behavior. Distance Range 5 - 200 meters Ability only triggers when the target is between 5m and 200m away. Projectile Count 1 Controls how many rocks are thrown per ability execution cycle. Cycle Mode Restart Cycle Restarts ability cycle after cooldown completes. Min / Max Attack Delay 1 second Cooldown time after ability completion before re-evaluating target distance. Power-up Animation Pick Animation clip played while retrieving the rock from the ground. Throw Animation Throw Animation clip played when launching the projectile.

NOTE: If Projectile Count is set to a high number (e.g., 30), the enemy will ignore the minimum distance limit (5m) and continuously throw rocks at close range until all 30 projectiles are fired. Setting Projectile Count = 1 forces the AI to finish the ability cycle after every single throw, allowing it to correctly re-check if the player has entered melee range (< 5m).

docs.title: 6. Rock Projectile & Damage Setup
docs.text: Configure the rock projectile object to travel along an arc and prevent self-collision triggering.

docs.title: Step 6.1: Projectile Setup
docs.text:
1. Open the Rock Projectile prefab in the Project inspector.
  2. Remove any obsolete components (e.g., remove Throwable Object Key if present).
  3. Confirm the following component configurations:
  4. Projectile Script:
    • Moving Delay: 0
    • Move Speed: 20
    • Move in Arc: Checked (Arc Type = Combined)
  5. Trigger Object Activator:
    • Delay Trigger: Checked
    • Activation Delay: 1.5 seconds
    • Purpose: Prevents rock fragments from hitting the spawner enemy's own triggers/colliders when spawned.
    • Auto Destroy: Enabled after 2 seconds.
  6. Hitbox Script:
    • Owner: Set to Rock Projectile
    • Activation Mode: Auto Activate On Start (Delay = 2 to 3 seconds)

docs.title: 7. Health UI, Impact FX & Death Behavior
docs.text: Configure impact particle systems and auto-cleanup upon death.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Expand Hit Reactions:
  2. Time To Destroy Spawn Impact Effect: 0.5 seconds.
  3. Impact Effect Hit: Replace default blood particle with Stones Hit FX asset.
  4. Expand Health & UI:
  5. Destroy Enemy On Die: Checked (Set delay to 5 seconds).
  6. Destroy Spawn Health Bar On Die: Checked.

docs.title: 8. Verification Checklist
docs.text:
Before running tests in Play Mode, check the following configuration settings:

  • [ ] Hand Socket Mapped: Right Hand bone transform assigned as Projectile Parent.
  • [ ] Spawn Point Assigned: Ground spawn point transform linked in Projectile Attack ability.
  • [ ] Projectile Count Set to 1: Prevents the enemy from ignoring minimum distance boundaries.
  • [ ] Arc Trajectory Active: Move in Arc enabled on Rock Projectile prefab.
  • [ ] Trigger Delay Active: Trigger Object Activator delay set to 1.5s to avoid self-collision.
  • [ ] Impact Particle Updated: Stones Hit FX assigned to Impact Effect Hit.
  • [ ] Cleanup Timers: Destroy Enemy On Die checked with a 5s destruction timer.

docs.title: Smart Turning Behaviour
docs.text: This guide demonstrates how to configure turning animations and target detection parameters on the Bull Boss enemy using the Boss AI Toolkit

docs.title: 1. Overview & Key Concepts
docs.text:
• Team Member System: Manages target detection and determines hostile vs. friendly entity relationships based on Team IDs
  • Enemy Vision Angle: Sets the field-of-view threshold (e.g., 45, 60) required to trigger turn animations
  • Mixamo Animation Workflow: Importing, configuring Humanoid rigs, and assigning root motion turning clips

docs.title: Step 1: Target & Team Setup
docs.text:
1. Select the Bull Boss New GameObject in your Unity hierarchy
  2. In the Inspector, navigate to Enemy Ability System.Expand Global Settings to locate the Team Member script
  3. Configure team relationships:
  4. Bull Boss: Set Team Name to Team2
  5. Player: Set Team Name to Team1

!!! NOTE "Team Relationship Rule" If both entities share the same team name (e.g., Team 2), they are treated as friendly and will not attack each other Differing team names establish hostility

  1. Assign target body parts (My Body Part to Target) for hit registration
  2. Set Target Detection Range to 100
  3. Check Auto Update Target (scans for nearby targets every 0.5–2.0 seconds)
  4. Uncheck Log Sorted Enemies

docs.title: Step 2: Rotation Settings
docs.text:
Under Global Settings, configure the following properties:

  • Detection Range: Set to 100 (matches the Team Member script)
  • Enemy Vision Angle: Set to 45
  • Initial Search Delay: Min 1, Max 2 seconds
  • Rotation Check Interval: 2
  • Rotation Speed: 1000

Enable the following checkboxes: - [x] Control Rotation - [x] Use Rotation Animation - [x] Always Look at Target - [x] Rotate Spine Bone

docs.title: Step 3: Mixamo Animation Setup
docs.text:
1. Search Mixamo for "Mutant Turn"
  2. Download Mutant Right Turn 90 (Unity format, With Skin)
  3. Toggle the Mirror checkbox on Mixamo to flip the clip, then download the Left Turn animation
  4. Drag both .fbx files into your Unity project
  5. Select both animation files and configure their Inspector settings:
  6. Rig Tab: Set Animation Type to Humanoid and Click Apply
  7. Animation Tab:
    • Rename clips to Right Turn and Left Turn
    • Set Based Upon (Root Transform Rotation) to Originaland Click Apply

docs.title: Step 4: Link Clips to Animator & Script
docs.text:
1. Select Bull Boss New and expand Animation Setup Script and Add Animation
  2. Drag Right Turn and Left Turn into their respective slots
  3. Assign parameter names:
  4. Right Animation Right Turn
  5. Left Animation Left Turn
  6. Click Add to Animator Controller and Optimize Animation Clips
  7. Under Rotation Animations, map the directions as follows:
Setting Right Direction Left Direction Direction Right Left Rotation Animation Right Turn Left Turn Idle Animation Idle Idle Use Root Motion Enabled Enabled Animation Duration 2 seconds 2 seconds

!!! Tip "Auto Duration" Click Auto Get Length to automatically populate the animation duration from the clip

docs.title: 3. Testing Vision Angles
docs.text: Vision Angle Behaviour Summary 45 Degrees Tight Response: The boss turns rapidly as soon as the player leaves its 45 Degrees, triggering quick micro-adjustments 60 Degrees Forgiving Margin: The player has a wider arc to maneuver without triggering turn animations, reducing overall turn frequency

docs.title: Spear Capturer Enemy Setup
docs.text: This setup provides a guide for setting up a ranged Throw and Capture Spear Enemy using the Boss AI Toolkit in Unity. It covers model setup, configuration cloning, custom Ragdoll physics creation, registering rotation animation parameters, custom ranged ability setup, and weapon capture mechanics.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Drag the 3D spear enemy model into the scene hierarchy.
  2. Remove any pre-existing Animator component on the model.
  3. Right-click the GameObject and select Prefab > Unpack Prefab Completely.
  4. Rename the GameObject to Throw and Capture Spear Enemy.
  5. Match the position transform values to align with the original source template prefab.
  6. Assign character materials to the model mesh.
  7. Duplicate the spear weapon asset and mount/position it under the character's Right Hand bone socket.

docs.title: 2. Cloning Enemy Configuration
docs.text: Duplicate configuration settings from the existing Throw and Capture template prefab.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Navigate to Tools > Boss AI Toolkit > Duplicate Enemy.
  2. Configure cloning settings:
  3. Source Boss: Drag in the template Throw and Capture enemy prefab.
  4. Target Boss: Drag in the newly prepared Throw and Capture Spear Enemy GameObject.
  5. New Boss Name: Set to Throw and Capture Spear Enemy.
  6. Avatar: Drag and drop the model's target Avatar asset.
  7. Animator Controller: Leave disabled/default to reuse the base prefab's existing animation controller asset.
  8. Click Start Cloning Configuration.
  9. Deactivate the old template prefab in the scene hierarchy.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Select Throw and Capture Spear Enemy in the hierarchy.
  2. Go to top menu: GameObject > 3D Object > Ragdoll...
  3. Drag the character's Animator component into the wizard field.
  4. Click Autofill to auto-assign limb bones (assign missing transforms manually if needed).
  5. Click Create.
  6. Fine-tune generated colliders (e.g., adjust head bone sphere collider dimensions).

docs.title: 4. Animation Setup Tool: Rotation Animations
docs.text: Register left and right turn animations into the Animator Controller for smooth turning.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Add the Animation Setup Tool component to Throw and Capture Spear Enemy if not already present.
  2. Assign the character's Animator Controller.
  3. Click Add Animation and register two turn parameters:
  4. Idle Turn Left clip -> Parameter Name: turn left
  5. Idle Turn Right clip -> Parameter Name: turn right
  6. Click Add to Animator.
  7. Under Enemy Ability System > Global Settings > Rotation Animations:
  8. Add 2 direction entries: Left (turn left) and Right (turn right).
  9. Click Auto Get Length to fetch default animation durations.
  10. Set idle animation reference and enable Apply Root Motion.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Select Throw and Capture Spear Enemy and expand Combat Attack System.
  2. Set distance limits: Min Distance = 5, Max Distance = 200.
  3. Behavior: The enemy will only throw the spear when the target is between 5m and 200m away. Moving closer than 5m forces melee/hit reactions instead of throwing.
  4. Expand Custom Ability:
  5. Ability Type: Set to Create Your Own Ability.
  6. Script Reference: Assign Enemy Throw Ability.
  7. Function: Select ActivateThrow.
  8. Ability Lifetime: 3 seconds (restarts ability after interval cooldown).
  9. Expand Enemy Weapon Throw Ability:
  10. Weapon To Throw: Drag the spear weapon transform from the right hand socket into this field.

docs.title: 6. Health UI & Death Settings
docs.text: Configure health bars and ragdoll death transitions.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Under Health & UI:
  2. Check Spawn Health Bar Prefab and assign the health bar UI prefab.
  3. Death Mode: Set to Die Using Ragdoll Physics.
  4. Under Hit Reactions:
  5. Set Time To Destroy Spawn Impact Effect to 0.5 seconds (ensures hit impact particles render properly on damage).
  6. Under Team Member:
  7. My Body Part To Target: Assign the enemy root mesh object reference.

docs.title: 7. Verification Checklist
docs.text:
Before running tests in Play Mode, check the following configuration settings:

  • [ ] Cloned Configuration: Setup cloned from Throw and Capture template prefab.
  • [ ] Ragdoll Created: Colliders and Rigidbodies generated via the 3D Ragdoll wizard.
  • [ ] Animator Parameters: turn left and turn right parameters added via the Animation Setup Tool.
  • [ ] Combat Range Limits: Ranged ability restricted to distances between 5 and 200 meters.
  • [ ] Weapon Reference: Spear transform assigned to Weapon To Throw field.
  • [ ] Death Mode Selected: Die Using Ragdoll Physics active in Health & UI.

docs.title: Spear Spawner Enemy Setup
docs.text: This setup provides a guide for setting up a ranged Spear Spawner Enemy using the Boss AI Toolkit in Unity. It covers model setup, configuration cloning, custom animation registration, projectile spawner setup, and projectile prefab configuration.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Drag the 3D spear spawner model into the scene hierarchy.
  2. Right-click the GameObject and select Prefab > Unpack Prefab Completely.
  3. Rename the GameObject to Spear Spawner Enemy New.
  4. Assign the required character material to the model mesh.

docs.title: 2. Cloning Enemy Configuration
docs.text: Duplicate configuration settings from the existing Spear Spawner Enemy template prefab.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Navigate to Tools > Boss AI Toolkit > Duplicate Enemy.
  2. Configure cloning settings:
  3. Source Boss: Drag in the template Spear Spawner Enemy prefab.
  4. Target Boss: Drag in the newly prepared Spear Spawner Enemy New GameObject.
  5. New Boss Name: Set to Spear Spawner Enemy New.
  6. Avatar: Drag and drop the model's target Avatar asset.
  7. Create New Animator Controller: Uncheck (reuses the base template's existing animation controller asset).
  8. Weapon: Uncheck.
  9. Click Start Cloning Configuration and close the window.

docs.title: 3. Global Settings & Rotation Animations
docs.text: Configure turning behaviors and register turning clips.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Select Spear Spawner Enemy New and expand Enemy Ability System > Global Settings:
  2. Use Rotation Animations: Checked.
  3. Rotate Spine: Unchecked.
  4. Under Rotation Animations, add two direction entries:
  5. Left: Choose the left turning clip (turn left), enable Apply Root Motion, and click Auto Get Length.
  6. Right: Choose the right turning clip (turn right), enable Apply Root Motion, and click Auto Get Length.

Note: If rotation animation clips are missing, add the Animation Setup Tool component to the enemy. Assign the Animator Controller, register the clips with parameter names, click Add to Animator Controller, and select them from the rotation animation dropdown.

docs.title: 4. Health UI & Hit Reactions
docs.text: Configure health UI, death modes, and hit response timings.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
• Health & UI:
  • Spawn Health Bar Prefab: Enabled (spawns an health bar).
  • Death Mode: Set to Die Using Animations. Add a dying animation clip and check Apply Root Motion. (Or set to Die Using Ragdoll Physics).
  • Hit Reactions:
  • Time To Destroy Spawn Impact Effect: 0.5 seconds.
  • Min / Max Hit Interval: 1 second.

docs.title: Step 5.1: Distance Group & Ability Setup
docs.text:
1. Under Combat Attack System, set Phase 0 Health Range (0 - 100) and Initial Attack Delay to 1 second.
  2. Create/edit a distance group with range 5 to 200 meters.
  3. Add an ability and set Ability Type to Projectile Attack.
  4. Set power-up duration and assign the Magic animation clip to play while spawning.

docs.title: Step 5.2: Spawn Point Setup
docs.text:
1. Create an empty child GameObject under Spear Spawner Enemy New named Spear Spawn Point.
  2. Position Spear Spawn Point in front of the enemy (copy transform from the template prefab).
  3. In the Projectile Attack settings panel:
  4. Spawn Point: Assign the Spear Spawn Point transform.
  5. Projectile Parent: Assign the Spear Spawn Point transform.
    • Purpose: Parenting ensures the spawned spear rotates and stays aligned with the enemy while targeting before it is thrown.

docs.title: 6. Spear Projectile Prefab Configuration
docs.text: Set up the projectile object and collision components.

docs.title: Projectile Alignment & Components
docs.text:
1. Mesh Orientation: Ensure the spear model's +Z axis (forward) points in the direction of movement.
  2. Team Member: Assign the Team Member component with the same team name as the enemy.
  3. Capsule Collider: Add a Capsule Collider and check Is Trigger.
  4. Hitbox Component:
  5. Set Owner to the spear itself and check Compare Enemy (assigning the spear's Team Member script).
  6. Auto Activate On Start: Checked.
  7. Deactivate Hitbox On Hit: Checked.
  8. Deactivate Hitbox After Time: Checked (5 seconds).
  9. Destroy Mode On Hit: Set to Destroy Owner (destroys the spear upon impacting the player).

docs.title: Projectile Script Settings
docs.text:
Parameter Value Description Moving Delay 0 Delay before movement begins. Move Speed 20 Forward travel velocity. Rotation Mode None Disables spinning/facing changes during flight. Move Forward Only Checked Forces the spear to fly straight ahead instead of tracking the player dynamically. Unparent On Move Checked Detaches the spear from Spear Spawn Point as soon as movement begins.
  1. Apply changes to the Projectile Prefab asset and assign it to the Projectile Prefab field on the enemy's attack ability.

docs.title: 7. Verification Checklist
docs.text:
Before running tests in Play Mode, check the following configuration settings:

  • [ ] Rotation Animations: Turn left and turn right parameters linked with root motion enabled.
  • [ ] UI & Hits: Spawn health bar enabled and hit impact effect destroy delay set to 0.5s.
  • [ ] Spawn Transforms: Spear Spawn Point assigned as both Spawn Point and Projectile Parent.
  • [ ] Projectile Alignment: Spear mesh Z-axis oriented forward.
  • [ ] Projectile Script Options: Move Forward Only and Unparent On Move checked on the spear prefab.

docs.title: Spit Attack
docs.text: This part guide on setting up the Spit Attack Ability on the Bull Boss using the Boss AI Toolkit in Unity. It covers ability configuration, particle system adjustments, trigger hitbox positioning, and animation timing.

docs.title: 1. Initial Ability Configuration
docs.text: Set up the Spit Attack parameters inside the Enemy Ability System and adjust combat range and probability for isolated testing.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Select the Bull Boss New GameObject in the scene hierarchy.
  2. Expand the Enemy Ability System component and locate the active phase group (e.g., Phase 0).
  3. Set Min Distance to 0 and Max Distance to 10 meters.
  4. Click Add Ability Entry to Group.
  5. Set Ability Type to Spit Attack.
  6. Set Spit Attack Probability to 100% for isolated testing.
  7. Configure core settings:
  8. Look Mode: Target
  9. Spit Attack Range: 10 meters

docs.title: 2. Animation Binding
docs.text: Bind the spit animation clip to the boss using the Animation Setup Tool.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Expand the Animation Setup Tool on the Bull Boss.
  2. Locate and select the Spit animation clip from your project directory.
  3. Click Add Animation and drag the Spit clip into the field.
  4. Set the parameter name to Spit.
  5. Click Add to Animator.
  6. Return to the Enemy Ability System -> Spit Attack settings and select Spit under Spit Animation.

docs.title: 3. VFX & Hitbox
docs.text: Create the visual particle effect combined with a trigger hitbox to deal damage within the spit cone.

docs.title: Step 3.1: Particle FX Setup
docs.text:
1. Search for the prefab Sparks Explode Green (located in Hovl Studio Magic Effects).
  2. Drag and drop it as a child under the Bull Boss New GameObject.
  3. Rename the object to Spit Attack Effects.
  4. Configure particle parameters:
  5. Duration: 1 second
  6. Looping: Uncheck (disable continuous looping)
  7. Scale: 0.8 on X, Y, and Z
  8. Shape: Set to Cone
  9. Rotation: 30° on X
  10. Angle: 35°
  11. Radius: 2
  12. Arc: 180°
  13. Unpack the prefab completely in the Hierarchy.

docs.title: Step 3.2: Damage Hitbox Setup
docs.text:
1. Right-click Spit Attack Effects -> Create Empty and name it Hitbox.
  2. Position the Hitbox object forward within the cone area where the spit effect lands.
  3. Click Add Component -> Sphere Collider:
  4. Check Is Trigger.
  5. Adjust radius size to cover the intended damage cone area.
  6. Click Add Component -> Hitbox:
  7. Damage: 10
  8. Owner: Drag the Bull Boss New GameObject.
  9. Compare Enemy: Checked
  10. Script Team Member: Drag the boss's Team Member script reference into this slot.
  11. Activation Mode: Auto Activate On Start
  12. Activation Delay: 0 seconds
  13. Check both default deactivation checkboxes.
  14. Deactivate the Spit Attack Effects GameObject in the scene hierarchy by default.

docs.title: 4. Activation Delay & Particle Timing
docs.text: Configure timing delays so the particle effect and hitbox align naturally with the spit animation keyframes.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
Select the Bull Boss New GameObject and set the following parameters under Spit Attack:

Parameter Value Description Spit Attack Effects Spit Attack Effects Reference to the child VFX/Hitbox container. Spit Attack Range 10 meters Maximum distance for ability execution. Spit Effect Activation Delay 1.6 seconds Delay during animation before enabling particles and hitbox. Spit Effect Particles Fade Time 1.2 seconds Active particle emission and duration before fading. Delay Before Idle 1 second Wait duration after ability completion before switching to idle. Idle Animation Idle Resting state animation clip.

docs.title: 5. Verification Checklist
docs.text:
Before testing the ability in Play Mode, check the following configuration settings:

  • [ ] Range Limits: Min/Max distance set to 0 - 10 meters to trigger close to the target.
  • [ ] Probability: Spit Attack set to 100%.
  • [ ] Animation Bound: Spit parameter registered in Animator and assigned in the ability slot.
  • [ ] VFX Active State: Spit Attack Effects is deactivated in the hierarchy by default.
  • [ ] Hitbox Ownership: Hitbox Owner linked to Bull Boss New with Compare Enemy checked.
  • [ ] Particle Alignment: Cone shape, angle (35°), radius (2), and scale (0.8) verified in forward direction.

docs.title: Summon Minions
docs.text: This setup provides a comprehensive guide for setting up the Summon Minions Ability on the Bull Boss using the Boss AI Toolkit in Unity. It covers core ability settings, VFX and teleport spawn location configurations, ground and aerial summoning modes, predefined spawn point setups, and ability sequence management.

docs.title: 1. Initial Ability & Proximity Setup
docs.text: Configure the Summon Minions ability inside the Enemy Ability System and adjust probability settings to isolate the ability during testing.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Select the Bull Boss New GameObject in your scene hierarchy.
  2. In the Enemy Ability System, expand the active Phase group.
  3. Adjust proximity parameters:
  4. Set Min Distance to 0 and Max Distance to 100 meters.
  5. Set existing ability probabilities (e.g., Spit Attack) to 0%.
  6. Click Add Ability Entry to Group.
  7. Set Ability Type to Summon Minions.
  8. Set Summon Minions Probability to 100% for isolated testing.
  9. Set Look Mode to Target.

docs.title: 2. Core Ability & Visual Effects Setup
docs.text: Configure the casting animation, aura effects, and delay settings for spawning minion entities.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Skip Check: Enable Skip If Spawned Enemies Exist to prevent summoning a new wave if previous minions are still active in the arena.
  2. Begin Animation: Assign the magic area animation clip.
  3. Casting Effect: Assign the Lightning Aura GameObject (active particle system during casting) to the Effect To Activate field:
  4. Set Effect Fade Out Duration to 3 seconds.
  5. Spawn Effect Prefab:
  6. Search for the Teleport effect prefab (Hovl Studio Magic Effects) in the Project folder.
  7. Assign Teleport to Spawn Location Effect Prefab.
  8. Set Spawn Location Effect Offset to 0.7 (elevates the effect slightly above ground level).
  9. Timing Delays:
  10. Set Spawn Effect Delay to 3 seconds (delay before showing teleport visual indicators).
  11. Set Delay Enemies Spawn After Effects to 0.5 seconds (delay between visual effect appearance and actual entity instantiation).
  12. Set Idle Delay to 1 second.

docs.title: 3. Minion Prefab & Placement Settings
docs.text: Specify the enemy prefabs to spawn and define their target proximity or sequential spawning options.

docs.title: Ground Spawn Configuration Options
docs.text: Parameter Recommended Value Description Enemies Prefab Knight Prefab Melee minion entity instantiated by the ability. Number of Enemies to Spawn 3 Total count of minion entities spawned per cast. Spawn Enemies Sequentially Unchecked If enabled, spawns assigned enemy prefabs one after another. Spawn Range From Target 20 meters Maximum radius around the player where minions spawn. Distance Between Each Spawned Enemy 5 meters Minimum spatial separation between individual spawned minions.

docs.title: 4. Predefined Spawn Points (Optional)
docs.text: Specify exact positional markers for minion spawning instead of using dynamic target-range spawning.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Right-click in the Hierarchy -> Create Empty and name it Predefined Enemy Spawn Points.
  2. Create three child empty GameObjects inside it:
  3. Predefined Enemy Spawn Point 1 (positioned left of the boss)
  4. Predefined Enemy Spawn Point 2 (positioned right of the boss)
  5. Predefined Enemy Spawn Point 3 (positioned behind the boss)
  6. (Optional) Parent Predefined Enemy Spawn Points under the Bull Boss New GameObject.
  7. Select Bull Boss New and locate the Summon Minions settings:
  8. Lock the Inspector window.
  9. Enable Spawn At Predefined Points.
  10. Drag all three point transforms into the Predefined Points array.
  11. Unlock the Inspector window.

docs.title: 5. Aerial Summoning Setup (Optional)
docs.text: Enable aerial capabilities to make the boss fly to a designated point before casting the summoning spell.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Navigate to Summon Minions settings on the Bull Boss New GameObject.
  2. Check Fly At Certain Point.
  3. Fly Target Point: Drag an existing elevated transform (e.g., Fly Point) into this slot.
  4. Set Fly Speed to 3.
  5. Set Fly Animation to Idle (or a dedicated hover animation).

docs.title: 6. Execution Sequencing
docs.text: Combine the Summon Minions ability with other combat abilities (e.g., Melee Attack) using sequential execution.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Under the active Phase group, set probabilities to 100% for both Summon Minions and Melee Attack.
  2. Check Play In Sequence.
  3. Reorder the ability list in the Inspector so Summon Minions is positioned at the top above Melee Attack.
  4. Upon execution, the boss will perform the Summon Minions ability first and transition into a Melee Attack once the spawn cycle completes.

docs.title: 7. Verification Checklist
docs.text:
Before running tests in Play Mode, verify the following configuration settings:

  • [ ] Proximity Limits: Group Min/Max distance set appropriately (0 - 100 meters).
  • [ ] Probabilities: Summon Minions set to 100% (and Play In Sequence checked if chaining abilities).
  • [ ] Prefabs & Effects: Teleport effect assigned to Spawn Location Effect Prefab and minion asset (Knight) assigned to Enemies Prefab.
  • [ ] Skip Check: Skip If Spawned Enemies Exist checked if single-wave spawning is desired.
  • [ ] Spawn Points: If Spawn At Predefined Points is enabled, verify all transform slots are populated.

docs.title: Teleportation
docs.text: This setup details how to configure the Teleportation Ability on the Bull Boss New AI entity. It covers target spawning cycles, particle effect setup, trigger collider exclusions, and integrating the shader dissolve controller.

docs.title: 1. Ability Core Configuration
docs.text: Add the Teleportation ability to the boss's ability system and configure its timing and targeting mechanics.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Select the Bull Boss New GameObject in your scene hierarchy.
  2. In the Inspector, locate the Enemy Ability System component.
  3. Click to Add Ability and select Teleportation.
  4. Remove any existing default events attached to this ability.
  5. Adjust probabilities to isolate testing:
  6. Set Teleportation Ability Probability to 100.
  7. Set Jump Attack Probability (and other abilities) to 0.
  8. Configure timing and positioning parameters:
  9. Disappear Animation Trigger: Set to Ground Slam (or Idle).
  10. Reappear Animation Trigger: Set to Idle.
  11. Disappear Delay: 3 seconds.
  12. Appear Delay: 3 seconds.
  13. Appear/Disappear Max Range: 15 meters.
  14. Total Teleport Cycles: 3.
  15. Spawn Location: Select preferred spawn strategies such as Spawn Behind Target, Spawn Left, or Spawn Right.
  16. Idle Delay: 2 seconds (delay before returning to normal behavior after cycles end).

Note: The boss will disappear after 3 seconds, perform 3 complete teleport cycles around the player within a 15-meter range, and then enter an idle state for 2 seconds.

docs.title: 2. Trigger Colliders & Range Visualization
docs.text: To prevent physics bugs or unwanted damage during teleportation, assign all active hitboxes/colliders to the ability setup.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. In the Inspector, lock the Inspector view on Bull Boss New.
  2. Locate the Colliders array inside the Teleportation ability parameters.
  3. Drag and drop all attached trigger colliders (e.g., the main character collider and weapon Damage Point colliders) into this list.
  4. (Optional) Check Visualize Range in Scene if you need scene view gizmos to see the 15-meter teleportation boundary.
  5. Unlock the Inspector view.

docs.title: 3. Visual FX (VFX) Setup
docs.text: Combine smoke and lightning particle systems into a single parent object to handle disappear and reappear visual effects.

docs.title: 3.1 Preparing the Particle Prefabs
docs.text:
1. Search for the Explosion prefab in Hovl Studio -> Prefabs -> Smoke Hits and Explosion.
  2. Unpack the prefab completely in your scene:
  3. Delete the Flash Shockwave child object.
  4. Remove the root Particle System component.
  5. Remove any extra explosion particle sub-objects, leaving only the Smoke particle system.
  6. Ensure Is Looping is Unchecked on the smoke particle component.
  7. Search for VFX Lightning in the project tab and bring it into the scene:
  8. Unpack the prefab completely.
  9. Adjust transform parameters: Scale to (0.5, 0.5, 0.5) and Rotation X to -90.

docs.title: 3.2 Creating the Combined VFX Parent
docs.text:
1. Right-click Bull Boss New -> Create Empty and name it Teleportation Effects.
  2. Make both the modified Smoke object and Lightning object children of Teleportation Effects.
  3. Ensure both child particle objects are active, but deactivate the parent Teleportation Effects GameObject by default.

docs.title: 3.3 Binding Effects to the Ability
docs.text:
1. Select Bull Boss New and locate the Teleportation ability settings.
  2. Enable both Disappear Effects and Appear Effects checkboxes.
  3. Drag and drop Teleportation Effects into both the Disappear Effect and Appear Effect fields.
  4. Set effect timings:
  5. Effect Activation Delay: 0 seconds (triggers immediately upon teleport start).
  6. Effect Active Lifetime: 1 second.

docs.title: 4. Dissolve Shader Event Hooks
docs.text: Integrate the Enemy Dissolve Controller to visually fade out the character mesh and weapon materials during teleportation.

docs.title: 4.1 Configuring Dissolve Parameters
docs.text:
In the Enemy Dissolve Controller component attached to the boss, set up four elements:

Element Name Shader Property Start Fill Amount Target Fill Amount Render Type Assigned Mesh Material Used Delay / Duration Dissolve In _DissolveAmount 0 1 Skinned Mesh Renderer Boss Mesh Bull Dissolve Delay: 0s, Duration: 1s Dissolve In Weapon _DissolveAmount 0 1 Mesh Renderer Weapon Mesh Spiky Weapon Dissolve Delay: 0s, Duration: 1s Dissolve Out _DissolveAmount 1 0 Skinned Mesh Renderer Boss Mesh Bull Dissolve Delay: 0s, Duration: 1s Dissolve Out Weapon _DissolveAmount 1 0 Mesh Renderer Weapon Mesh Spiky Weapon Dissolve Delay: 0s, Duration: 1s

Crucial Note: Ensure the Original Material field on Dissolve Out points to the Bull Dissolve material instead of standard materials to prevent the character model from turning plain white upon reappearing.

docs.title: 4.2 Binding Event Hooks
docs.text:
1. Locate Event Hook Listener on Bull Boss New and add two new event hooks:
  2. Hook 1: On Disappear
  3. Target: Drag Enemy Dissolve Controller.
  4. Function: EnemyDissolveController -> SetFillByName.
  5. String Parameter: Enter Dissolve In.
  6. Add a second entry targeting Enemy Dissolve Controller -> SetFillByName with parameter Dissolve In Weapon.
  7. Hook 2: On Appear
  8. Target: Drag Enemy Dissolve Controller.
  9. Function: EnemyDissolveController -> SetFillByName.
  10. String Parameter: Enter Dissolve Out.
  11. Add a second entry targeting Enemy Dissolve Controller -> SetFillByName with parameter Dissolve Out Weapon.

docs.title: 5. Verification Checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] Probabilities: Teleportation is set to 100%, other abilities set to 0% for testing.
  • [ ] Colliders: All character and weapon Hitbox colliders are assigned in the ability parameters.
  • [ ] VFX Parent State: Teleportation Effects parent object is deactivated in hierarchy by default.
  • [ ] Particle Loops: Particle systems under Teleportation Effects have Is Looping unchecked.

docs.title: Throw Objects
docs.text: This setup provides a step-by-step guide on setting up the Throw Objects Ability for the Bull Boss using the Boss AI Toolkit. It covers ability binding, weapon unequipping/equipping logic, hand-carried object synchronization, destruction setup, arc trajectories, and full animation configurations.

docs.title: 1. Initial Ability Configuration
docs.text: Set up the advanced custom ability inside the Enemy Ability System and isolate its probability for testing.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Select the Bull Boss New GameObject in your scene hierarchy.
  2. Expand the Enemy Ability System component in the Inspector.
  3. Click Add Ability Entry to Group.
  4. Set Ability Type to Create Your Own Ability Advanced.
  5. Set Ability Name to Throw Objects.
  6. Add Script: Drag and drop the Enemy Throwable Object Ability script.
  7. Set Function: Select Activate Throwable Attack.
  8. Set Ability Lifetime to 10 seconds.
  9. Adjust probabilities for isolated testing:
  10. Set Throw Objects Probability to 100%.
  11. Set all other ability probabilities to 0%.
  12. Adjust detection distance under general ability settings:
    • Set Min Distance to 0 and Max Distance to 50 meters (ensures reachable objects are detected across the area).

docs.title: 2. Core Ability Settings & References Setup
docs.text: Assign the core component references and target search conditions on the Enemy Throwable Object Ability component.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. In the Inspector for Enemy Throwable Object Ability, assign the following references:
  2. Team Member: Drag the boss's Team Member script.
  3. Animator: Drag the boss's Animator component.
  4. Nav Mesh Agent: Drag the boss's NavMeshAgent component.
  5. Pickup Bone: Drag the boss's Right Hand transform (where weapons are held).
  6. Configure search conditions:
  7. Search Mode: Find Closest Throwable Objects (or Find Random Throwable Objects).
  8. Throwable Object Tag: Set to ThrowableItems.
  9. Search Range: 50 meters.

docs.title: 3. Hand-Carried Object & Back Weapon Setup
docs.text: To create a seamless transition where the boss un-equips its weapon, picks up an object, throws it, and re-equips its weapon, you must configure carried references.

docs.title: Step 3.1: Hand-Carried Object (Visual Placeholder)
docs.text:
1. Locate the scene throwable object (e.g., a stone tagged Throwable Items with a Throwable Object Key set to stone).
  2. Duplicate the stone and make it a child of the boss's Right Hand bone.
  3. Reset its local position, scale it appropriately, and clean up unnecessary components:
  4. Remove NavMeshModifier and NavMeshObstacle.
  5. Set tag to Untagged.
  6. Ensure Throwable Object Key script is attached with the key set to Stone.
  7. Rename the object to Stone and deactivate it by default.

docs.title: Step 3.2: Back Weapon (Holstered Visual)
docs.text:
1. Duplicate the main Weapon GameObject on the boss's hand.
  2. Parent it under the Spine_02 bone transform and align it on the boss's back.
  3. Rename it to Weapon Back and deactivate it by default.
  4. On the Enemy Throwable Object Ability script:
  5. Assign the active weapon to Assign Weapon.
  6. Assign Weapon Back to Back Weapon Transform.

docs.title: 4. Animation Setup & Disarm Logic
docs.text: Download necessary disarm/equip animations from Mixamo and configure timing logic.

docs.title: Step 4.1: Import & Setup Mixamo Animations
docs.text:
1. Download Standing Disarm (Unequip) and Unarmed Equip Over Shoulder (Equip) animations from Mixamo (Humanoid rig).
  2. In Unity, set animation Rig type to Humanoid, check Bake into Pose, and set Based Upon to Original.
  3. Open the Animation Setup Tool on the Bull Boss.
  4. Add and name the animation parameters:
  5. Pickup (Pickup animation)
  6. Throw (Throw animation)
  7. Unequip Weapon (Standing disarm animation)
  8. Equip Weapon (Unarmed equip animation)
  9. Click Add to Animator.

docs.title: Step 4.2: Timing & Delay Settings Configuration
docs.text:
Click Add Config on the Enemy Throwable Object Ability script and configure the timing parameters:
